name: Fortress Loans Chain price feed submit() without validator verification
summary: Chain.submit() accepts a caller-supplied price array with caller-supplied signatures and never rejects signers that hold no validator stake, so any address can set any feed value. In one transaction the attacker executed a queued governance proposal that made fFTS collateral, called submit() to set FTS/USD to 4e34, and borrowed every Fortress market dry against 5,000 fFTS minted from 100 FTS.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0x586c43e5b4661aff337a3424dfafec4fb81d00570da3bb4a161b51f7aa0ba62d both at the deployment block 13441159 and at block 17634662, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

Every component is the net token movement of the exploit contract 0xcd337b920678cf35143322ab31ab8977c3463a45 in the single exploit transaction, plus its native BNB balance, which goes from 0 at block 17634662 to 1224.650634144094162737 at block 17634663. Attacker-side inputs are excluded: 100 FTS and 3.02030953619907 MAHA were paid in, and the 5,000 fFTS and 2,000,000,000 ARTH.usd received are protocol receipt tokens with no external market. DefiLlama observations lie within 65 seconds of the incident timestamp; the four stablecoins use par, whose largest deviation from the DefiLlama observation is 0.25 percent. Contemporary reporting put the loss near USD 3 million, which is above this exact onchain sum; the difference is valuation method, not additional transfers.
